- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) or shows negative spikes, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% for next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >3%), model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after recent highs), model tends to lag; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per day for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 1.00), model overfits short-term trends; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in 30d forecast.  
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14d moving average, model is biased; adjust forecast toward 14d MA for next 7 days.  
- If sentiment history includes multiple 1.00 entries (strong bullish), model often fails to account for eventual correction; reduce forecast by 1–2% per 3–5 day horizon.  
- If true outcome shows downward trend after 3+ consecutive bullish sentiment days, model tends to overestimate; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day for 5–7 days.
